lesson_title: The Headline and the Till Slip
hook_text: Bank A shouts 9,4%. Bank B whispers 9,3%. Bank B pays you more. Here's the small print trick matric maths teaches you to beat.
clip_script: Two banks fight for your money. Bank A's window shouts nine comma four percent a year. Bank B's window says nine comma three — but compounded quarterly. Everyone picks A, right? Wrong — and the reason is the difference between the window sticker and the till slip. That advertised number is the NOMINAL rate — a headline. The EFFECTIVE rate is what your money actually grows by in a full year, small print included. Get it by sending one rand through the machine. Bank B splits its nine comma three into four little paydays of about two comma three percent a quarter — and every payday's interest starts earning interest immediately. One rand becomes one comma zero-nine-six. That's an effective nine comma SIX-THREE percent. Bank A? Pays once a year — its till slip is exactly nine comma four. B beats A. The quieter sticker wins. That's the whole exam skill: never compare stickers. Convert every offer to its till slip — the effective rate — then compare like with like. Banks bet you'll read the big number and skip the small print. Matric maths is how you call the bluff.
visual_style: Two neon bank storefronts face off; window stickers flash big percentages while animated till slips print the true rates, coins split into quarterly paydays that snowball, and the underdog bank's slip stamps the win.
pacing: Punchy duel setup, slow-motion reveal of the small print, accelerating payday snowball, mic-drop verdict.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never be fooled by a headline rate again.
